rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Gymnosperms are seed plants with naked (exposed) seeds, not enclosed in fruits. They reproduce via cones; Pinus is the NEB model. Pollination is wind-based (anemophilous); no flowers or nectar are involved. The life cycle has a dominant sporophyte and a reduced gametophyte. Gymnosperms are economically important in Nepal as timber (Deodar, Pine), resin sources, ornamentals, and sacred trees.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Life cycle: Microsporangium → Microspore (n) → Pollen (male gametophyte)
Megasporangium → Megaspore (n) → Female gametophyte (archegonia)
Pollination: Pollen → Ovule (on cone scale) → Fertilisation (no water needed)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Gymnosperms produce SEEDS but NOT fruits; angiosperms produce both seeds AND fruits.  ·  Gymnosperm seeds are "naked" (exposed on cone scales); angiosperm seeds are enclosed in a fruit.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects a labelled diagram of Pinus male and female cones.  ·  The key distinction: gymnosperms = naked seeds (no fruit); angiosperms = enclosed seeds (fruit).

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Pinus merkusii — conifer, gymnosperm; wind-pollinated; produces resin and timber.  ·  Deodar (Cedrus deodara) — Himalayan conifer; sacred tree; timber and ornamental.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Pinus is wind-pollinated (anemophilous); no flowers or nectar are involved.  ·  Gymnosperms do NOT undergo double fertilisation; that is unique to angiosperms.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Gymnosperms: seeds NOT enclosed in fruit; naked seeds on cone scales.  ·  No true flowers; reproduction via cones (strobili).  ·  Pinus: wind-pollinated; male cones produce pollen; female cones bear ovules.  ·  Life cycle: sporophyte dominant; gametophyte reduced, non-photosynthetic.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Gymnosperms appeared ~300 million years ago (Carboniferous); they dominated the Mesozoic era.  ·  Pinus is wind-pollinated; a single male cone can release millions of pollen grains.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Gymnosperms: seed plants with "naked" seeds (seeds not enclosed in a fruit); include conifers (Pinus, Deodar), ginkgo, cycads, and gnetophytes.  ·  Body: woody stem (trunk), needle-like or scale-like leaves; no true flowers; reproduction via cones (strobili).  ·  Pinus (model): conifer; male cones (pollen cones) produce microspores → pollen grains; female cones (seed cones) produce ovules → seeds after pollination.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Seed: Embryo + Endosperm + Seed coat (no fruit)  ·  No double fertilisation (unlike angiosperms).  ·  Economic: timber, resin, ornamental, soil, sacred trees (Deodar).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Deodar (Cedrus deodara) and Pine (Pinus) are both conifers in the family Pinaceae; they differ in leaf form (needle-like vs scale-like) and cone structure.  ·  Gymnosperms have a dominant sporophyte; the gametophyte is reduced and non-photosynthetic.  ·  Deodar (Cedrus deodara) is a sacred Himalayan tree; its economic and cultural importance is a common application question.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Pinus is wind-pollinated; no insect or water is needed for pollination.  ·  Memorise the structure of Pinus male and female cones.  ·  Learn the gymnosperm life cycle (no water needed for fertilisation).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: List economic importance of gymnosperms in Nepal (timber, resin, ornamental).  ·  Note the cultural significance of Deodar in Nepali tradition.  ·  Gymnosperms are the first seed-bearing plants to evolve.
